# Additional context

* Write markdown files to provide additional context for agents
* Primary motivation:
  * Avoid repeating yourself across multiple conversations
  * Save tokens by avoiding common mistakes
* We'll focus on `AGENTS.md` (always loaded) and skills (loaded on demand)
* Lets dive in with an example

# `AGENTS.md`

## Let's make a package, take two

(Make sure you're in normal mode)

```R
usethis::create_package("~/desktop/compliment2")
usethis::use_tidy_agents()
```

> Create a new R package called compliment in the current directory. It should generate randomized compliments.

## Your turn

* Try it yourself. What differences do you notice in the workflow?
* Read `AGENTS.md`. What advice does it contain?

## Where does it live?

* Project level: `AGENTS.md` in the project root
  * Checked into git; shared with your whole team
  * Applies to everything below it in the directory tree
* User level: `~/.posit/assistant/AGENTS.md`
  * Personal preferences that apply across all your projects
* Project (generally) beats user when they conflict
* If you're using Claude you also need `CLAUDE.md` that contains `@AGENTS.md`

## What belongs there?

* Have you told an agent to do it three times? Put it in `AGENTS.md`
* Is it a lot of text that is only sometimes important? Use a skill.

# Skills

## Your turn

* `use_tidy_agents()` includes three skills. What are they? How do they work?
* What do you think the advantages and disadvantages of distributing of skills this way?

## What is a skill?

* Formal definition at <https://agentskills.io/>
* But IMO this is very overwrought
* Two parts to a skill:
  * When: short description that states when to use it
  * What: longer details of how to use it
* System prompt includes all the "when"s
* Agent loads the "what" on demand

## Other forms of skills

* Directory of markdown files with index/README
* [Quarto website](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-llms.html) 
  * Use `llms-text: true` 
  * Basic idea: <https://design.tidyverse.org>
* R documentation
* R functions

## General advice

* Hold on to them loosely
* Keep them personal, local, timely
* Best for stuff a general LLM can't know
* Relatively little benefit to using same model to both write and read
* They don't have to be markdown files

## Winston's simplification prompt

<!-- Extracted from https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/blob/main/.agents/skills/assistant-review/SKILL.md -->

Make a deliberate pass over each non-trivial change looking for opportunities for simplification:

* Could this change be achieved by deleting or restructuring instead of adding — removing a branch, mode, layer, or special case rather than bolting one on? It's always better to remove than add.

* Is each new or changed interface narrow relative to what it hides — or must callers know its internals, keep duplicated logic in sync, or work around documented gaps ("does NOT handle X")?

* Does anything re-implement what the codebase already provides — a bespoke helper shadowing a canonical one, logic in the wrong layer, or wrapper/cast/any churn obscuring the real contract?

When you find opportunities for simplification, be clear about the pros and cons. Produce either a list of potential simplifications or "No simplifications found".

## Bundling with a package

* No automated tooling yet
* `inst/skills` is a reasonable place to put them
* You'll need to expose in some other way
